items.claim: Negative bleed empties one axis, so the copy cap passes and the other axis's loop stalls the frame
Bare-number `bleed` widens only x, so content tiled in y pops in at the top and bottom edges
items.note: This was a behavior call nobody had made, so I made it and recorded it in `docs/unruled.md`: a bare bleed now covers both axes, while a bare period still wraps x only. A lattice tiled on x alone draws as before.

items.claim: `plane.set({ pan: undefined })` stores `undefined` over the pan and every later draw throws
items.note: This was also a behavior call, recorded in `docs/unruled.md`: an undefined `pan` in a patch leaves the pan as it was. I didn't make it throw, because an animator's `set({ pan: maybe })` means "no change", not misuse. An undefined `zoom` or `anchor` still resets it to its default.
